question: do i get a break if im doing a 7 hour shift? how long for
reference_answer: If daily working time is more than six hours, a worker is entitled to an uninterrupted rest break of at least 20 minutes, which they can spend away from their workstation, unless a collective or workforce agreement sets different terms (WTR 1998 reg. 12(1)-(3)).

question: finished at 1am after a late close and the rota has me back in at 9am. is that even allowed??
reference_answer: No. A worker is entitled to at least 11 consecutive hours' rest in each 24-hour period (12 hours for young workers), and 1am to 9am is only 8 hours (WTR 1998 reg. 10).

question: how many days off am i meant to get a week? ive just done 9 days straight
reference_answer: An uninterrupted 24 hours in each 7-day period, or, if the employer chooses, two 24-hour periods or one 48-hour period in each 14 days (WTR 1998 reg. 11(1)-(2)).

question: whats minimum wage for a 19 year old atm
reference_answer: £10.85 an hour for workers aged 18 to 20 (National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 reg. 4A(1)(b)).

question: my boss doesnt give us payslips, the money just goes in the bank. is that allowed
reference_answer: Yes. A worker has the right to a written itemised pay statement at or before each payment of wages, showing gross pay, deductions and their purposes, and net pay (ERA 1996 s. 8).

question: started at a new restaurant 3 weeks ago and still havent got a contract or anything in writing. when are they meant to give me one
reference_answer: The written statement of particulars must be given no later than the start of the employment (ERA 1996 s. 1(1) and (2)(b)).

question: im on zero hours at a cafe and they said i cant pick up shifts at another restaurant. can they actually stop me
reference_answer: No. Any term of a zero hours contract that prohibits the worker from working under another contract, or requires the employer's consent to do so, is unenforceable against the worker (ERA 1996 s. 27A).

question: chef told us to plate up basa when the menu says cod. is that illegal?
reference_answer: Selling, to the purchaser's prejudice, food that is not of the nature, substance or quality demanded is an offence (Food Safety Act 1990 s. 14).

question: i live in at the hotel i work at and they take rent out of my wages. how much of that can count towards minimum wage?
reference_answer: For minimum wage purposes the accommodation offset is £11.10 for each day accommodation is provided; charges above that reduce pay when checking it meets the minimum wage (NMW Regulations 2015 regs. 14 and 16).

question: been at the same pub 3 years and theyre letting me go. how much notice do they have to give me
reference_answer: At least 3 weeks: one week for each complete year of continuous employment between 2 and 12 years (ERA 1996 s. 86(1)(b)).

question: im 17 and do 6 hour shifts at the weekend. what breaks do i get and how long do i need off between shifts
reference_answer: A young worker working more than 4.5 hours is entitled to a 30-minute break (reg. 12(4)), and to 12 consecutive hours' rest in each 24-hour period (reg. 10(2)) (WTR 1998).

question: how much paid holiday do you get a year if youre full time?
reference_answer: 5.6 weeks: 4 weeks under reg. 13 plus 1.6 weeks of additional leave under reg. 13A, capped at 28 days (WTR 1998).

question: can my work use our tips to make our pay up to minimum wage?
reference_answer: No. Tips, gratuities and service charges paid through the employer do not count towards minimum wage pay (NMW Regulations 2015 reg. 10(m)), and qualifying tips must be allocated fairly between workers (ERA 1996 s. 27D).

question: till was £50 down at the end of my shift and my manager says its coming out of my wages. can they do that?
reference_answer: Only if the deduction is authorised by the contract or agreed in writing beforehand (ERA 1996 s. 13), and for workers serving the public (retail employment, s. 17) deductions for cash shortages cannot exceed one tenth of gross wages on any pay day (s. 18).

question: how much sick pay will i get if im off ill for a week
reference_answer: Not answerable from the sources: they say workers may be entitled to Statutory Sick Pay, but do not give the amount or how it is calculated.

question: my manager says we only get a break if we work over 8 hours. is that right?
reference_answer: No. The right to a rest break (at least 20 minutes) applies once daily working time is more than six hours (WTR 1998 reg. 12(1) and (3)).

question: my boss says theyre allowed to keep half the tips because its their business. thats right isnt it
reference_answer: No. The employer must ensure the total amount of qualifying tips, gratuities and service charges is allocated fairly between workers, and amounts allocated to a worker are payable to them (ERA 1996 s. 27D(1)-(2)).

question: im on zero hours so i dont get holiday pay right?
reference_answer: Wrong: zero-hours workers are entitled to statutory paid annual leave. A worker whose paid hours are wholly or mostly variable is an irregular hours worker (WTR 1998 reg. 15F(1)(a)), and accrues leave at 12.07% of hours worked in each pay period (reg. 15B).
